Maya to share benchmark plan and synthetic dataset generator by 2025-03-18
Schedule 2-hour pilot benchmark run wk of 2025-03-24
Customer to provide sample prompt logs and PII examples by 2025-03-17
action_items: Alex Chen - Send security + retention doc - 2025-03-14
Maya Patel - Prepare benchmark script and synthetic dataset - 2025-03-18

header: Fireflies Transcript - 2025-03-11 16:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Maya Patel, Ben Ortiz, Jordan Reyes (Redwood) — Samantha Lee, Dr. Amir Qureshi, Miguel Torres, Priya Nair (Horizon HealthTech)
summary: POC scoping kickoff to lock down data handling constraints for a 4-week POC. Main topics: PII redaction options, logging vs ephemeral prompt handling, retention windows, benchmark plan (workload sizing + metrics), timeline and success criteria. High-level decision: prefer hosted dedicated pool with redaction pipeline and configurable short retention for logs; security docs requested.
topics: Benchmark workload sizing and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, Alex from Redwood here, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call?
[00:18] Samantha Lee: Samantha here, Head of Data at Horizon.
[00:22] Dr. Amir Qureshi: Amir, CPO.
[00:25] Miguel Torres: Miguel, ML Eng.
[00:27] Priya Nair: Priya, legal.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Maya from Redwood SE team. Ben and Jordan are on the call as well.
[00:32] Alex Chen: Yeah cool, goal for today is to scope the POC: how you want prompts handled, what we can log, retention windows, and a benchmark plan so we can agree success criteria.
[01:10] Samantha Lee: To set the context, we're in healthcare, so PHI/PII is the big blocker. We need assurance that no raw PHI is stored unencrypted or kept longer than necessary. Our initial use case is clinical triage notes — average prompt length ~140 tokens, bursty traffic during business hours. We'll run a POC to validate latency and accuracy.
[01:58] Maya Patel: Understood. A few early options: 1) full logging for the POC (on a short retention e.g., 7 days) with guaranteed redaction before longer-term storage, 2) no logging — ephemeral only — which limits debugging, or 3) redact at ingestion (PII detection) and keep redacted logs. We can show you how each impacts debugging and cost.
[02:34] Dr. Amir Qureshi: Important: redaction needs to be deterministic and auditable. We can't rely solely on heuristic redaction; need to see confidence thresholds and allow export of redaction audit logs.
[03:05] Alex Chen: Noted. We have an ingestion agent that can run a PII classifier (names, MRN, DOB, SSN patterns) and either mask or hash identified tokens. It's plumbed into our hosted API or Dedicated deployments. Small caveat — sometimes transcripts will show mis-tags, e.g., "Redwood" sometimes transcribed as "Red wood" in automated logs — sorry, that's my demo brain — but you get the idea.
[03:45] Miguel Torres: How does that interact with prompt caching / KV cache? We rely on prefix caching for cost. If you redact at ingestion, does caching still match?
[04:12] Maya Patel: Good call. For correctness, we can do cache keys on the normalized/redacted prompt. So the KV cache/hash is computed after normalization which avoids leaking raw PII into caches. There is a tradeoff: redaction reduces cache hits if the redaction is too aggressive and yields many unique normalized forms.
[04:58] Samantha Lee: What's the default retention on hosted logs? Do you store prompts persistently?
[05:12] Alex Chen: Default for hosted is 30 days for debugging, but we have options: 7 days, 90 days, or disabled. For Private deployments you control retention entirely. For Dedicated, we can set the policy per workspace. For the POC we can set 7 days to limit exposure.
[05:45] Priya Nair: Encryption at rest and KMS access — can customer manage keys?
[05:52] Jordan Reyes: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer KMS in certain regions. We'll follow up with exact regions and the KMS providers supported.
[06:16] Dr. Amir Qureshi: We also need to make sure function calls and tool outputs aren't inadvertently logged. For example, if the model calls a 3rd party or outputs a URL with identifying info, that has to be filtered.
[06:42] Maya Patel: We can configure output filters and set the logging level per route: none, redacted, full. Filtering is driven by regex and ML-based PII detectors; we can include a rule set you provide that catches internal PHI patterns.
[07:05] Miguel Torres: Benchmarking — what metrics do you need? We'll want p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k tokens, and model output quality (top-N accuracy on a labeled set). For triage, latency p95 target is <300ms ideally, but we can accept <500ms for the POC.
[07:45] Maya Patel: Great. For sizing, tell us concurrency and average sequence lengths. Samantha said ~140 tokens average, do you have concurrent session estimates?
[07:58] Samantha Lee: We see up to 60 concurrent agents at peak, but typical sustained concurrent is about 18. Peak bursts up to 120 queries/min. Daily volume initial POC estimate ~80k tokens/day.
[08:25] Alex Chen: For a quick pilot we'll emulate peak bursts: 60 concurrent, 140 tokens avg, 5 RPS sustained ramping to 20 RPS bursts. For a hosted Dedicated pool, we recommend X GPUs (we'll propose configs) — for the POC we'll provision a small dedicated pool so you get predictable latency.
[08:55] Miguel Torres: Would you be able to run the pilot against an open-weights quantized variant? We want to measure quality delta and cost improvement.
[09:08] Maya Patel: Yes, we can run the same prompt set against a float32 baseline and a 4-bit quant model. We'll provide quantization/quality metrics. Expect some small degradation on nuanced outputs; we'll pair that with your eval set.
[09:35] Samantha Lee: On success criteria: 1) P95 latency <500ms under the POC workload, 2) cost under our budget — roughly $0.50 per 1k tokens — and 3) no unredacted PHI leaves the system. Also accuracy on clinical intent detection must be >= 92% on the labeled set.
[10:10] Alex Chen: Good clear success criteria — we'll bake those into the benchmark. We'll also instrument regression alerts if accuracy dips during runs.
[10:25] Priya Nair: Legal wants an audit trail of who viewed logs and redaction operations. Can you provide role-based access and audit logs?
[10:35] Ben Ortiz: Yes, RBAC is supported. Audit logs record access to logs and who triggered redaction overrides. For the POC, we can give limited read-only access to a small group.
[11:00] Dr. Amir Qureshi: I want to confirm that prompt storage policy can be configured per route — for example triage-route keep 7 days redacted logs, feedback-route ephemeral only.
[11:21] Maya Patel: Correct. Route-level policy and tenant-level defaults. Policies support retention windows and whether to keep raw prompts, redacted prompts, or nothing.
[11:40] Miguel Torres: How do you handle deleting cached keys if retention is set to zero? If logs are disabled does the KV cache still persist?
[11:58] Alex Chen: KV cache is independent; by default cache is in memory and ephemeral per node. We can configure cache eviction and not persist cache to disk. If you want absolute assurance, we can disable cross-request caching persistence and only use in-flight caches.
[12:25] Samantha Lee: Are transcripts used to train models? We must have a guarantee they are not used to train any public models.
[12:35] Jordan Reyes: We do not use customer prompts to train our public models. For hosted offerings we offer an explicit opt-out and enterprise customers have contractual language preventing any training use. We'll share contract language.
[13:00] Priya Nair: We'll need SOC2 Type II, and also some HIPAA alignment doc.
[13:10] Alex Chen: We'll attach SOC2 and a HIPAA readiness checklist. Note our Private offering is the preferred path if you require full HIPAA BAAs; our legal team will follow up.
[13:35] Samantha Lee: For the POC dataset, how should we send data? We prefer an anonymized sample set containing redacted PHI tokens, but also a small set with synthetic PHI-like tokens so your redaction can be validated.
[13:55] Maya Patel: That works — synthetic PHI is ideal for debugging. We'll provide a script to synthesize names, MRNs, and dates so you don't have to share real PHI.
[14:20] Miguel Torres: On the benchmark script: can you support streaming responses? Our product uses streaming to show partial answers. That impacts latency measurements and concurrency behavior.
[14:35] Maya Patel: Yes, we test both streaming and non-streaming. Streaming can change p95 patterns; we'll include both.
[15:05] Alex Chen: Let's align on the pilot steps and timeline: week 0 — finalize scope and sign off on retention settings and sample dataset; week 1 — campaign build and environment provisioning; week 2 — run benchmark & quality evals; week 3 — review results and iterate. So roughly a 3–4 week POC. Does that fit your expectations?
[15:35] Samantha Lee: Yes that's reasonable. If results look good, we may accelerate to a short-term Dedicated reservation.
[15:50] Dr. Amir Qureshi: On redaction evaluation — we'll want metrics: false positives (removed non-PII), false negatives (missed PII), and time-to-redaction.
[16:05] Maya Patel: We can produce a redaction evaluation report per run that includes those stats. We also keep an audit trail of redaction decisions with anonymized examples.
[16:38] Miguel Torres: Will the PII detector run inline (synchronous) or as an async job? Sync adds latency; async risks a window where raw prompt is processed before redaction.
[16:58] Maya Patel: We support both. For your use case the recommended approach is synchronous redaction at ingestion so nothing raw hits downstream systems; the tradeoff is a small added latency ~20–60ms depending on rule set. We'll measure this in the pilot.
[17:25] Samantha Lee: That extra 20–60ms is acceptable if it guarantees no raw PHI persistence.
[17:35] Alex Chen: We'll instrument the redaction step and include the latency delta in the benchmark outputs.
[17:50] Priya Nair: About encryption and KMS: if customer-managed keys are used, do you support key rotation and key access logs?
[18:05] Jordan Reyes: Yes, key rotation is supported and access logs are emitted to the customer's KMS audit logs. We'll provide a tech note with supported KMS providers and regions.
[18:30] Miguel Torres: For cost measurement, can you break down token billing vs infra cost so we can see delta when using quantized models?
[18:45] Maya Patel: We'll provide a token-level cost breakdown and per-GPU-hour infra burn. For quantized models we'll show the inference speed and cost per 1k tokens.
[19:05] Samantha Lee: If we do ephemeral-only logs for the feedback route, can we still run offline quality evals? We need some labeled outputs to validate.
[19:20] Alex Chen: Yes — for offline QA we can run a separate evaluation mode that writes outputs to an encrypted, short-lived bucket that you control. That way operational logs remain ephemeral but you can still validate.
[19:42] Dr. Amir Qureshi: Any limitations on region/data residency? We need EU residency for some patient cohorts.
[19:55] Jordan Reyes: We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region options in US and EU; we'll confirm specific availability for your account.
[20:18] Miguel Torres: When you redact, do you replace with placeholders (e.g., [NAME_REMOVED]) or pseudonymize with consistent hashes? The latter helps for dialogues involving the same patient across messages.
[20:36] Maya Patel: We support both. Pseudonymization with stable hashing allows correlation without exposing PHI; masked placeholders are easier for debugging. You can choose per-route.
[21:02] Samantha Lee: We prefer pseudonymization for triage context.
[21:12] Alex Chen: Noted — we'll set that as default for the triage route.
[21:25] Priya Nair: Legal will want an export of redaction rules and an attestation of how redaction works for the contract.
[21:35] Ben Ortiz: We'll prepare an overview doc and a sample attestation. For full legal language, our contracts team will handle BAA/BPA language.
[21:55] Miguel Torres: On technicalities: does your runtime ever spill KV cache to persistent store for warm restarts? We need to ensure that doesn't leak PHI accidentally.
[22:12] Jordan Reyes: Default is in-memory only. For warm restarts some deployments snapshot caches; we can disable snapshotting for your POC or ensure snapshots are encrypted and stored with customer KMS.
[22:40] Samantha Lee: For the benchmark dataset, we'll prepare three sets: synthetic PHI, redacted real prompts, and a small labeled evaluation set with gold intents.
[22:55] Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll give you the generator script. We'll also provide a sample harness to run the 2-hour stress test.
[23:20] Alex Chen: Two more things: will you require SSO/SCIM and RBAC integration for the POC?
[23:34] Samantha Lee: Yes, SSO via SAML is required for our administrators.
[23:40] Ben Ortiz: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll send setup steps.
[24:02] Dr. Amir Qureshi: Does your platform record who executes redaction overrides? We need that audit trail.
[24:12] Ben Ortiz: Yes, overrides are logged with user and timestamp.
[24:27] Miguel Torres: A small nit — when you said "prefix caching" earlier, is that the same as the " KV cache " in the docs? I saw a note about "kay-vee cache" in the last export and wasn't sure.
[24:40] Maya Patel: Yeah sorry our internal notes sometimes read out weirdly — KV cache is key-value cache. We'll include a doc that maps terms.
[25:00] Samantha Lee: Okay let's re-confirm concrete success criteria for the POC so legal and procurement are happy:
[25:11] Samantha Lee: 1) No unredacted PHI in logs or backups, 2) P95 latency <500ms for the triage route at defined load, 3) Model intent accuracy >=92% on the labeled test set, 4) Redaction FN rate <1% and FP rate <5% on test samples.
[25:45] Alex Chen: We'll make those explicit in the benchmark plan.
[26:00] Priya Nair: Procurement will still want an SLA for the pilot? Minimum availability?
[26:08] Ben Ortiz: For pilots we typically commit to operational support but not full SLA; if you move to Dedicated reservation, we can sign an SLA. We'll note that in the follow-up.
[26:30] Miguel Torres: About test harness — can the script simulate variable prompt templates? E.g., redacted placeholders, clinical codes, and short/long prompts.
[26:44] Maya Patel: Absolutely, the generator supports templating and variable lengths. We'll give you a few templates used in past healthcare pilots.
[27:02] Samantha Lee: On the timeline again: can we start provisioning week of 3/24? We need a signed POC addendum before then.
[27:12] Alex Chen: Yes — we aim to provision as soon as the addendum is signed and we have the sample dataset.
[27:28] Dr. Amir Qureshi: For compliance, does Redwood have any HIPAA-specific certifications or partners you rely on?
[27:40] Jordan Reyes: We don't claim HIPAA certification per se; our Private and Dedicated offerings are designed to support HIPAA compliance and we offer BAAs for enterprise customers. We'll route you to legal for details.
[28:05] Samantha Lee: If we find redaction misses during the pilot, what's the remediation process?
[28:12] Maya Patel: We'll do immediate hotfixes to rules, re-run the failing batch, and produce an incident report. We'll also tag those examples for model/PII detector retraining if you opt into that. Any retraining would be under your control and with explicit opt-in.
[28:45] Miguel Torres: For metrics, will you provide a dashboard during the run?
[28:52] Ben Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console will have a per-route dashboard showing latency, token burn, redaction stats, and error rates. We can give read-only access to your team.
[29:10] Samantha Lee: Can we get a sample dashboard before the POC?
[29:16] Ben Ortiz: We'll share a template and access to a sandbox.
[29:30] Alex Chen: I'm going to summarize next steps then: 1) Alex will send SOC2 + security one-pager and retention options by 3/14; 2) Maya will share benchmark plan, harness, and synthetic data generator by 3/18; 3) Samantha will provide sample logs (anonymized) and a small labeled eval set by 3/17; 4) schedule the pilot 2-hour benchmark wk of 3/24; 5) legal will review BAA/attestation language.
[30:12] Priya Nair: Sounds good. One more question — are you able to provide a snapshot of your redaction classifier precision/recall on healthcare templates?
[30:24] Maya Patel: We have baseline numbers from past pilots; we'll include those with caveats. We'll also run the detector against your synthetic set during the pre-provision step.
[30:40] Samantha Lee: Any blocker on our side? We need the addendum signed and the synthetic dataset.
[30:48] Alex Chen: No blockers from Redwood beyond those items.
[31:00] Miguel Torres: Quick note — for the evaluation, can we run both streaming and non-streaming at same concurrency to compare?
[31:10] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll configure parallel runs.
[31:28] Samantha Lee: Okay thanks everyone. If you could put the action items in email after the call that'd be great.
[31:36] Alex Chen: Will do. Ben will follow up with the dashboard link and Jordan will send KMS region support.
[31:50] Ben Ortiz: I'll include read-only console access for the sandbox.
[32:05] Priya Nair: We'll review the contract team and circle back with any legal edits by 3/20.
[32:18] Alex Chen: Great. Any final questions?
[32:24] Dr. Amir Qureshi: None from me.
[32:26] Miguel Torres: All good.
[32:28] Samantha Lee: Thanks, appreciate it.
[32:30] Alex Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with docs and the plan.
[32:35] [Meeting ends]

Note: transcription contains small mis-hearings and occasional punctuation issues as per standard Fireflies exports.
